examples.en: In spring, cherry blossoms are in full bloom in the park.
Roses were in full bloom in the garden.

examples.ko: 꽃이 만발한 길을 걸으면 기분이 좋아요.
examples.en: Walking down a road full of blooming flowers feels good.

examples.ko: 산에 진달래가 만발할 때 등산을 가요.
examples.en: I go hiking when azaleas are in full bloom on the mountain.

examples.ko: 유채꽃이 만발하는 제주도에 가 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to visit Jeju, where rape blossoms bloom everywhere.
The cosmos were in full bloom, so I took many photos.

explain: '피다'는 꽃 한 송이에도 쓰지만, '만발하다'는 꽃이 가득 핀 풍경에 써요. 주로 글이나 방송에서 쓰는 느낌이고, '꽃이 만발하다'처럼 꽃 이름과 같이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '활짝 피었어요'를 더 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: The cherry blossoms are in full bloom in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 비슷하고 일상 대화에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, and more common in everyday talk.

phrases.en: I walked slowly along a road full of blooming flowers.
phrases.nuance_ko: '만발한' 뒤에 장소를 붙여 풍경을 그릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a place after 만발한 to paint a scene.

phrases.example: 벚꽃이 만발할 때 사진을 찍으러 가요.
phrases.en: I go take photos when the cherry blossoms are in full bloom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃이 가장 예쁘게 핀 때를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the time when flowers are at their prettiest.

explain_en: Many flowers blooming all over a place (벚꽃이 만발하다) '피다' can describe a single flower, but '만발하다' describes a scene full of blossoms. It sounds more like writing or broadcasts, and pairs with flowers: '꽃이 만발하다'. In daily talk, people say '활짝 피었어요'.

t90.ax: Roses were in full bloom in the garden.

examples.ko: 들판에 백마 한 마리가 서 있어요.
examples.en: A white horse stands in the field.

examples.ko: 동화 속 왕자는 백마를 타고 와요.
examples.en: The prince in fairy tales comes riding a white horse.
A white horse has fur as white as snow.
The child drew a picture of a white horse.
I once saw a white horse on Jeju Island.
That white horse is the one my uncle raises.

explain: 일상에서는 '하얀 말'이라고 하고, '백마'는 이야기나 글에서 더 자주 보여요. 동화 속 왕자는 보통 백마를 타요. '백'은 하얗다는 뜻의 한자어예요.

phrases.example: 백마 탄 왕자님을 기다리지 말고 스스로 길을 찾아요.
phrases.en: prince on a white horse; Prince Charming
phrases.nuance_ko: 이상형이나 나를 구해 줄 완벽한 사람을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an ideal partner or a perfect person who will come to rescue you.

explain_en: In daily talk people say 하얀 말, while 백마 appears more in stories and writing. A prince in a fairy tale usually rides a 백마. The 백 part is a Sino-Korean element meaning white.

examples.en: Lightning flashed and soon the rain poured down.

examples.ko: 어두운 방에서 휴대폰 화면이 번쩍여서 잠이 깼어요.
examples.en: The phone screen flashed in the dark room and woke me up.
A light flashed right in front of me and startled me.
My new watch glitters in the sunlight.

examples.ko: 카메라 플래시가 번쩍이는 순간 눈을 감았어요.
examples.en: I closed my eyes the moment the camera flash went off.
The child's eyes lit up with curiosity.

explain: 번개나 플래시처럼 순간적으로 강하게 빛나는 것에 써요. '번쩍거리다'와 거의 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 눈이 '번쩍 뜨이다'처럼 '번쩍'만 따로 쓰는 표현도 많아요.

phrases.en: The lightning kept flashing, so I was scared.
phrases.nuance_ko: '번쩍이다'와 거의 같은 뜻이라 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as 번쩍이다, so they can be used interchangeably.

phrases.en: The flashing light dazzled my eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸밀 때는 '-는'을 붙여서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -는 to modify a noun that follows.

phrases.en: My eyes snapped open at the sound of the alarm.
phrases.nuance_ko: '번쩍'만 따로 써서 갑자기 눈이 뜨이는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 번쩍 alone to describe eyes suddenly opening.

explain_en: Near-synonym of 번쩍거리다; shorter 이다 form, can be a single flash or repeated. It is used for things that flash strongly for a moment, such as lightning or a camera flash. It can almost always be swapped with '번쩍거리다'. The bare '번쩍' also appears in set expressions such as '눈이 번쩍 뜨이다' (eyes snap open).

t90.ax: My new watch glitters in the sunlight.

examples.en: I picked up a starfish at the beach.

examples.ko: 불가사리는 팔이 다섯 개인 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: Many starfish have five arms.

examples.ko: 물이 빠지자 바위 위에 불가사리가 보였어요.
examples.en: When the water went out, I saw a starfish on the rocks.
My child likes starfish-shaped toys.

examples.ko: 불가사리처럼 생긴 별 모양 쿠키를 구웠어요.
examples.en: I baked star-shaped cookies that look like starfish.

examples.ko: 수족관에서 불가사리에게 먹이를 주는 체험을 했어요.
examples.en: I had an experience feeding the starfish at the aquarium.

explain: 바다 생물 말고도 옛이야기에 나오는, 쇠를 먹는다는 괴물의 이름도 '불가사리'예요. 보통 대화에서는 바다의 별 모양 생물을 말해요.

phrases.en: The children touched a starfish on the tidal flat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바닷가 체험에서 자주 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for beach activities.

phrases.en: I looked at the starfish stuck to the rock.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불가사리가 있는 장소를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say where a starfish is.
phrases.en_equiv: a starfish stuck to a rock

phrases.example: 별 모양 불가사리가 모래 위에 있었어요.
phrases.en: A star-shaped starfish was lying on the sand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모양을 설명할 때 '별 모양'과 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Combine with 별 모양 to describe its shape.

explain_en: Besides the sea animal, '불가사리' is also the name of a monster in old Korean tales that eats iron. In everyday conversation it usually means the star-shaped sea creature.

en: to burn; to blaze; to be aflame

examples.en: The whole mountain went up in flames in an instant.
I watched the firewood blaze for a long time.
The cheering heat blazed up at the final.
It felt like my chest was burning with anger.
The sky blazes red in the evening glow.

examples.ko: 그 불씨가 커져서 곧 불타오를 거예요.
examples.en: That spark will grow and soon burst into flames.

explain: 불타오르다는 '불타다'보다 불길이 위로 세게 일어나는 느낌이에요. 불 말고도 감정이나 열기가 거세질 때 '의욕이 불타오르다'처럼 비유로 많이 써요. '르' 불규칙이라 '불타올라요', '불타올랐어요'로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: The firewood is burning brightly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체 활용이라 말할 때 바로 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite present form, ready to use in speech.

phrases.en: Fire trucks came after seeing the blazing building.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 뒤의 '건물'을 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-는' lets it describe the noun '건물' after it.

phrases.en: Starting a new job makes my motivation burn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불이 아니라 마음이 강해질 때의 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for strong feeling, not real fire.

explain_en: Fire or passion rising and growing stronger. 불타오르다 feels more like flames rising fiercely than plain '불타다'. It is also used figuratively for feelings and excitement, as in '의욕이 불타오르다'. It is a 르-irregular verb: '불타올라요', '불타올랐어요'.

t90.ax: The sky blazes red in the evening glow.

examples.en: The hunter went up the mountain with his hunting dog.

examples.ko: 이 사냥개는 냄새를 아주 잘 맡아요.
examples.en: This hound has a very good sense of smell.
The hound ran off chasing a rabbit.

examples.ko: 옆집 사냥개는 낯선 사람을 보면 짖어요.
examples.en: The neighbor's hunting dog barks when it sees a stranger.

examples.ko: 사냥개를 훈련시키는 데 시간이 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes a long time to train a hunting dog.
The hunting dog in the movie is really cool.

explain: 일하는 개 이름은 '사냥개', '경찰견', '안내견'처럼 '-개'와 '-견'이 섞여 있어서 따로 익히는 게 좋아요. '권력의 사냥개'처럼 쓰면 시키는 대로만 움직이는 사람을 낮춰 부르는 말이 되기도 해요.

phrases.en: My grandfather raises hunting dogs in the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사냥에 쓰는 개를 기른다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means raising dogs used for hunting.

phrases.en: A hunting dog barked loudly in the forest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사냥개가 동물을 찾았을 때 나는 소리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the sound a hunting dog makes, such as when it finds prey.

phrases.en: Training a hunting dog takes a very long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사냥개를 가르치는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to teaching a dog to hunt.

explain_en: Names for working dogs mix '-개' and '-견', as in '사냥개', '경찰견', '안내견', so it's best to learn each one. In a phrase like '권력의 사냥개' (a hound of power), it can put down someone who just does as told.

en: to be gloomy; to be dull; to be cloudy

examples.en: The sky is gloomy today.

examples.ko: 벽 색이 우중충해서 방이 어두워 보여요.
examples.en: The wall color is dull, so the room looks dark.
On gloomy days, my mood sinks too.
Isn't the color of the clothes too drab?
It's the rainy season, so the weather has been gloomy for days.

examples.ko: 우중충하던 골목이 밝은 벽화 덕분에 환해졌어요.
examples.en: The gloomy alley became bright thanks to a cheerful mural.

explain: 날씨뿐 아니라 방, 옷 색, 분위기가 어둡고 칙칙할 때도 써요. '칙칙하다'와 비슷하고 '화창하다'와 반대되는 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 우중충한 날씨 때문에 기분이 안 좋아요.
phrases.en: The gloomy weather puts me in a bad mood.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 형태로 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 써요. 흐리고 어두운 날씨에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form before a noun; fits cloudy, dark weather.

phrases.en: The color of this outfit looks dull.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷이나 방의 색이 칙칙하게 느껴질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the color of clothes or a room feels dull.

phrases.en: The sky isn't gloomy today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 날씨가 맑거나 밝다는 뜻을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says the weather or place is not gloomy.

explain_en: Gloomy-looking sky, weather, or colors; spoken (우중충한 날씨) It describes not only weather but also rooms, clothing colors or moods that look dark and dull. It is close to '칙칙하다' and is the opposite of '화창하다' (bright and sunny).

examples.en: On Parents' Day, I pinned a carnation on my parents.
Carnations are most often red.
On Teachers' Day, I gave my teacher a carnation.
I bought a bunch of carnations at the flower shop.

examples.ko: 카네이션 한 송이만 있어도 마음이 전해져요.
examples.en: Even a single carnation conveys your heart.
My mother showed off the carnation pinned on her chest.

explain: 한국에서는 5월 8일 어버이날과 5월 15일 스승의 날에 특히 많이 주고받아요. 부모님 가슴에 빨간 카네이션을 달아 드리는 풍습이 있어요. '카네이션을 달다', '카네이션을 드리다'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 어머니 가슴에 빨간 카네이션을 달아 드렸어요.
phrases.en: I pinned a red carnation on my mother's chest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어버이날 꽃으로 가장 흔한 색이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common color for Parents' Day.

phrases.en: I gave my teacher a carnation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃은 '송이'로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Flowers are counted with 송이.

phrases.en: I bought a bouquet of carnations and went home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 송이를 묶은 선물을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For a gift of several carnations tied together.

explain_en: In Korea carnations are especially common on Parents' Day (May 8) and Teachers' Day (May 15). There is a custom of pinning a red carnation on a parent's chest. Use '카네이션을 달다' or '카네이션을 드리다'.

examples.en: I heard a hyena making a laughing sound at the zoo.
Hyenas hunt in packs.

examples.ko: 아프리카에서 하이에나와 사자가 싸우는 영상을 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched a video of a hyena and a lion fighting in Africa.

examples.ko: 하이에나는 다른 동물이 남긴 먹이도 먹어요.
examples.en: Hyenas also eat food that other animals leave behind.

examples.ko: 아이가 하이에나 그림을 그려서 벽에 붙였어요.
examples.en: The child drew a hyena and stuck it on the wall.

examples.ko: 만화에 나오는 하이에나는 늘 나쁜 역이에요.
examples.en: The hyena in cartoons is always the bad guy.

explain: '하이에나'는 아프리카에 사는 동물이에요. 한국어에서는 남이 애써 얻은 것을 노리는 사람을 '하이에나 같다'고 부정적으로 비유해서 말하기도 해요. 동물원이나 다큐멘터리에서 무리 지어 사냥하고 우는 소리가 사람 웃음 같다고 자주 소개돼요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 남의 성과만 노리는 하이에나 같아요.
phrases.en: to be like a hyena
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물 자체가 아니라, 남의 것을 노리고 빼앗으려는 사람을 부정적으로 비유하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is not about the animal; it negatively describes someone who preys on others' gains.

explain_en: '하이에나' is an animal of Africa. In Korean, someone who goes after what others worked hard for can be negatively called '하이에나 같다'. In zoos and documentaries it is often introduced as hunting in packs and making a sound like laughter.

examples.en: I got stung by a jellyfish while swimming in the sea.
I watched transparent jellyfish at the aquarium.

examples.ko: 여름에는 해파리가 많아서 바다에 못 들어가요.
examples.en: In summer there are many jellyfish, so you can't go into the sea.

examples.ko: 해파리 냉채는 중국 요리에서 자주 먹어요.
examples.en: Jellyfish cold salad is often eaten in Chinese cuisine.

examples.ko: 해파리는 뼈가 없고 몸이 거의 물이에요.
examples.en: A jellyfish has no bones and its body is almost all water.
Jellyfish float slowly in the water.

explain: 해변에 '해파리 주의' 안내가 붙을 만큼 여름 바다에서 자주 듣는 말이에요. 쏘이면 '해파리에 쏘이다'라고 해요. 음식으로는 '해파리냉채'로 먹기도 해요.

phrases.en: I got stung on the leg by a jellyfish while swimming.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해파리와 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말로, 피해를 입었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, used when someone is stung.
phrases.en_equiv: to get stung by a jellyfish

phrases.example: 해변에 해파리 주의 안내가 붙어 있어요.
phrases.en: A jellyfish warning sign is posted on the beach.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바닷가 안내문에서 자주 보는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often seen on beach signs.

phrases.en: I ordered jellyfish salad at the restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해파리로 만든 차가운 음식 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of a cold dish made from jellyfish.

explain_en: You hear this word a lot at summer beaches, where signs warn 해파리 주의. If one stings you, say 해파리에 쏘이다. It is also eaten as 해파리냉채.

examples.ko: 삽으로 땅을 파자 큰 흙덩이가 올라왔어요.
examples.en: When I dug the ground with a shovel, a big clod of earth came up.
The child plays by crumbling a clod of earth with their hands.
Lots of clumps of dirt stuck to the bottom of my shoes.

examples.ko: 나무를 옮길 때는 뿌리째 흙덩이를 함께 파야 해요.
examples.en: When moving a tree, you have to dig up the root ball with the soil.

examples.ko: 화분을 갈 때 단단히 굳은 흙덩이는 풀어 주세요.
examples.en: When repotting, break up any hardened lumps of soil.
The thrown clod of dirt hit the wall and broke apart.

explain: 흙이 한 덩어리로 뭉친 것이라서 '밭의 흙덩이', '신발에 붙은 흙덩이'처럼 작은 단위로 말해요. 흙이 많이 쌓인 것은 '흙더미'라고 해요. '흙덩어리'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: There are many clods of earth in the field.
phrases.nuance_ko: '흙덩이'와 뜻이 같고 조금 더 길게 말하는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '흙덩이', just a slightly longer form.

phrases.en: I broke up the clods of earth with a shovel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밭일을 할 때 뭉친 흙을 깨는 모습에 잘 맞아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits farm work where you break up hardened soil.

phrases.en: A lump of dirt stuck to my shoe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뭉친 흙이 어디에 붙어 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a lump of dirt is stuck to something.

explain_en: It means soil clumped into a single lump, so you use it for small units such as a clod in a field or dirt stuck to a shoe. Soil piled up in large amounts is '흙더미'. It is also said as '흙덩어리'.

examples.en: At an amusement park, I feel like a child again.
A child's drawing is full of a child's innocence.

examples.ko: 어른이 되어도 동심을 잃지 않고 싶어요.
examples.en: Even as an adult, I don't want to lose my childlike heart.
This fairy tale stirs the childlike heart in adults.
When it snowed, my childlike spirit came back.

examples.ko: 동심을 지켜 주고 싶어서 거짓말을 못 했어요.
examples.en: I wanted to protect the child's innocence, so I couldn't lie.

explain: 어린아이처럼 순수하고 깨끗한 마음이에요. '동심으로 돌아가다', '동심을 잃다', '동심을 지키다'처럼 써요. '천진난만'과 비슷하지만, 그건 아이의 모습 자체에, '동심'은 마음에 초점이 있어요.

phrases.en: When you become an adult, it's easy to lose your childlike heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 순수한 마음이 없어졌다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the pure, childlike heart is gone.

phrases.en: I want to protect children's innocence.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이의 순수한 마음을 다치지 않게 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means keeping a child's pure heart from being hurt.

phrases.en: This fairy tale is full of childlike innocence.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그림, 이야기, 노래가 순수한 느낌일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a picture, story, or song feels pure and childlike.

explain_en: 동심 is the pure, unspoiled heart of a child. It goes with 동심으로 돌아가다, 동심을 잃다 and 동심을 지키다. 천진난만 is similar but describes the child's look and manner, while 동심 focuses on the mind.

en: to rub off; to come off; to show through

examples.en: I touched the wall and paint rubbed off on my hand.

examples.ko: 검은 가방 색이 청바지에 묻어나서 속상해요.
examples.en: I'm upset because the black bag's color rubbed off on my jeans.
Warmth comes through in the way he speaks.
She sang in a voice that carried sadness.

examples.ko: 빨래할 때 색이 묻어나지 않게 따로 빨아요.
examples.en: I wash them separately so the color doesn't run onto others.
It's a painting that shows traces of long effort.

explain: 묻은 것이 다른 곳으로 옮겨질 때도 쓰고, 말투·글·표정에서 마음이나 분위기가 느껴질 때도 써요. 앞의 뜻은 '묻다'(물감이 묻다)와 가깝고, 뒤의 뜻은 '배어나다', '드러나다'와 비슷해요.

phrases.example: 새 청바지는 색이 묻어날 수 있어요.
phrases.en: The color of new jeans can come off on other things.
phrases.nuance_ko: 묻은 색이나 물감이 다른 곳으로 옮겨질 때 '색이 묻어나다'라고 구체적으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to say specifically that color or dye rubs off onto something else.

phrases.en: This lipstick doesn't come off on cups.
phrases.nuance_ko: '묻어나다'의 부정형이에요. 물건이 번지거나 옮겨 가지 않는다고 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used to say something does not smear or transfer.

phrases.en: Tiredness comes through in his way of speaking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 아니라 마음이나 분위기가 말투, 표정, 글에서 느껴질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a feeling or mood shows through speech, expression, or writing, not a physical stain.
phrases.en_equiv: to come through in one's tone

explain_en: Something transfers onto another surface; figuratively feelings show (슬픔이 묻어나다) It is used when something sticky or colored transfers onto another surface, and also when feeling or mood comes through in speech, writing, or expression. The first sense is close to 묻다 as in 물감이 묻다, and the second is similar to 배어나다 and 드러나다.
